<thought>Based on the mass spectrum, the neutral molecular mass is about 140 Da, which fits the formula C₈H₁₂O₂ (exact mass 140.0837 Da). The ¹³C NMR shows eight distinct carbon signals: a carbonyl (~167 ppm), two sp² carbons (~144 and 130 ppm), two equivalent aliphatic carbons (~34.5 ppm), and three different methyl carbons (~22.8, 21.3, 19.2 ppm). The ¹H NMR consists of three singlets (3 H, 6 H, 6 H), consistent with three types of methyl groups and no coupled protons. These data point to a highly symmetric, fully substituted molecule containing an ester carbonyl and no CH groups besides methyls. A plausible structure that matches C₈H₁₂O₂ and the NMR pattern is methyl 2,4‑dimethyl‑2‑butenoate (SMILES: **CC(C)=C(C)C(=O)OC**). This molecule has an ester carbonyl, two equivalent sp² carbons, three distinct methyl groups (one allylic, two vinylic), and the observed singlet proton signals.
